_comment: Shot list and narration for the b0b.dev intro film (site/intro-reel.mp4 +
site/intro-reel.js), built by scripts/build-intro-reel.py.
EVERY SHOT IS PUBLIC DOMAIN OR CC0 AND CARRIES ITS OWN CITATION. Each entry
names the archive item, a licence URL taken from that item's own metadata,
and the exact in-point, so the film can be rebuilt frame for frame by anyone
who runs the script, and the source line on screen names the item while it
plays. Footage nobody can trace is worth what a claim nobody can check is.
THE SOUND UNDER THE NARRATION IS THE FILMS' OWN: newsreel commentary, the
launch, the crowd, the room. Nothing was scored under it. It is level-matched
(loudnorm) and faded at each splice so seven sources recorded forty years
apart do not lurch; that is correction, not embellishment.
THE PICTURE IS CUT AND SCALED AND NOTHING ELSE - no grade, no retime, no crop
for drama. Grain, scanlines and vignette are drawn over it in the overlay.
THE NARRATION is spoken live by the reader's own browser in a British female
voice (see intro.js pickVoice), so it is real speech on every device and is
always on screen as text as well. Every line was checked against the record
before it went in; the ones that tempted a broader claim were narrowed:
Explorer 1 carried a cosmic-ray counter, not a camera, and the reconnaissance
programme came later under the cover name Discoverer (CORONA, first recovery
Aug 1960, declassified Feb 1995); the peace-march reel is quoted by its own
title ('Thousands'), not by a crowd estimate; and the placement of the
counter-demonstrators is 'in the same reel', which is what the film shows.
Captions date the NEWSREEL, not the event: Universal's Nuremberg reel was
released 6 Dec 1945, the trial opened 20 Nov 1945; Explorer 1 launched
31 Jan 1958 and the reel is dated 3 Feb 1958.

lines.text: Nuremberg, 1945.
The prosecution did not argue from rumour.
It put the documents on the table, drew the structure of a state on a board, and entered it as an exhibit.
Anyone in the room could check it.
That is the oldest rule in this archive, and the only method this report claims: show the record, say where it came from, and let the reader test it.
Washington, 1947.
A committee of Congress turned its instrument on citizens, and the newsreel cameras came with it.
Whether an inquiry is looking for facts or for a target is not settled by calling it a hearing.
It is settled by one question: could the finding have come out the other way?
Enewetak Atoll, 1952.
The first full-scale test of a thermonuclear device.
The capability arrives before the argument about what it is for.
This report records what a document establishes about a capability, and stops there.
Secrecy is evidence of nothing about what is hidden.
Cape Canaveral, 1958. The first American satellite.
It carried a cosmic-ray counter, not a camera.
The watching came two years later, under another name, and stayed classified for thirty-five.
A launch is documented the day it happens. What a thing is for is documented separately, by a different kind of paper, often decades later.
October, 1962.
A reconnaissance photograph becomes evidence the moment somebody labels it.
Three missile trailers. Cylindrical object.
The label is the claim, and the label is the part that has to be checked.
That is true of every caption in this report, including the ones on this film.
April, 1967.
Thousands against the war, and, in the same reel, their opponents, with placards of their own. The newsreel filmed both.
Discount the evidence that hurts your case exactly as hard as the evidence that helps it.
A crowd is testimony: evidence of an experience, never, by itself, evidence of a cause.
Washington, 1987. The inquiry, afterwards.
Everything in this report arrived the same way: late, in public, and on the record.
{TOTAL} documented sites. Twenty-four sections.
Every source named. Every tier stated.
The specimens it could not prove, killed on its own page.
The authority of a document does not come from what it alleges.
It comes from what it refuses to allege.
τετέλεσται — it has been completed, and remains so.
